articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, shaking the AI giant. The scandal highlights governance issues and the male hubris in Silicon Valley, raising concerns about succession and trust in AI leaders.

articles.headline: New obesity definition uses BMI, other body measurements
articles.summary: Researchers propose a new obesity definition combining BMI with waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio, distinguishing between clinical and preclinical obesity. This approach aims to improve diagnosis and tailored treatment for lifestyle diseases.

articles.headline: When Ramayana is recast for a franchise age
articles.summary: This opinion piece contrasts Ramanand Sagar's traditional Ramayana with Namit Malhotra's modern adaptation, arguing the latter "Disneyfies" the epic by removing key elements like Ravan's lust and Ram's longing to create a family-friendly franchise for global export.

articles.headline: Avril Lavigne welcomes first child, a baby girl
articles.summary: Pop-punk icon Avril Lavigne and her partner have welcomed their first child, a baby girl.

articles.headline: Furniture gets artsy shape-up in affluent homes
articles.summary: Affluent homeowners are embracing sculptural, custom-crafted furniture as art, moving beyond catalogue-inspired interiors. Curved sofas, distinctive consoles, and unconventional light fixtures are popular, valued for form, materials, and craftsmanship over mere functionality.

articles.headline: Heritage fashion steps back into focus
articles.summary: Fashion's nostalgia for craftsmanship is reviving heritage fabrics, archival patterns, and vintage-inspired silhouettes. Designers are updating classics with fresh proportions and tactile textures, reflected in rising searches for checked jackets and jacquard coats.

articles.headline: Retain Diwali glow: Layered lighting for homes
articles.summary: This lifestyle piece advocates for retaining the "Diwali glow" by adopting layered lighting, rather than relying on harsh overhead fixtures. It suggests using lower-level, warm-white lights (2700K) from table lamps and sconces to create a more inviting home ambiance.

articles.headline: Movie legends reunite for Steven Spielberg tribute
articles.summary: Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, and Robert De Niro reunited at MoMA’s 18th annual Film Benefit, which honored Spielberg. Tom Cruise also made a surprise appearance, praising Spielberg's generosity and support throughout his career.

articles.headline: Moose Wala’s family alleges song released without consent
articles.summary: Parents of late Punjabi singer Sidhu Moose Wala objected to the release of his song "Phantom," claiming it was unauthorized. They urged artistes and labels to consult them regarding his music rights, citing previous disputes over posthumous releases.

articles.headline: Taylor Swift to return to CMA stage after 13 years
articles.summary: Taylor Swift will perform at the Country Music Association (CMA) Awards on November 18, marking her first appearance in 13 years. She is also nominated for Single of the Year for her song "I Knew It, I Knew You."

articles.headline: Timely care for premature babies is crucial: Experts
articles.summary: Experts stress continued care and early stimulation for preterm babies, noting India's neonatal mortality rate decline, but preterm birth remains leading cause. Follow-up until at least five years, aided by AI, is vital for physical and neurodevelopmental health.

articles.headline: Add versatility to your meals with avocados
articles.summary: Avocados are highlighted as a nutritious and versatile addition to daily meals, offering heart-healthy fats, vitamins K, E, C, and dietary fiber. Their creamy texture makes them easy to incorporate into various dishes from parathas to salads.

articles.headline: Bengaluru rolls out red carpet for Lambodhara 2.0 premiere
articles.summary: Bengaluru hosted a grand red-carpet premiere for the film "Lambodhara 2.0," with an eclectic mix of corporate, political, film, and fashion personalities attending. Debutant writer-producer-actor Anil Shetty shared insights on his challenging transition into filmmaking.

articles.headline: KPop Demon Hunters fictional group announces world tour
articles.summary: HUNTR/X, the fictional K-pop group from "KPop Demon Hunters," will embark on a "Golden World Tour" starting June 2027. The tour will cover nearly 50 cities and over 150 shows across 2027 and 2028, bringing the film's elements to live audiences.

articles.headline: Wanted Groom - Shreya Sur seeks partner
articles.summary: Shreya Sur, a 30-year-old from Kolkata now in Mumbai, seeks a partner for a marriage built on friendship, mutual understanding, and shared values. She values family, personal space, and hopes for a liberal, nurturing environment for her future family.

articles.headline: Upendra and Sudhindra households celebrate wedding festivities
articles.summary: Niranjan Sudhindra is set to marry Sanjana, with pre-wedding festivities including a haldi shastra. The family, including actors Upendra and Priyanka Upendra, are celebrating the first wedding of the next generation with energetic dances and a grand mehendi ceremony.

articles.headline: Celebs give capri pants a stylish spin
articles.summary: Capri pants are making a comeback in celebrity wardrobes, styled in fresh, contemporary ways. Bollywood stars like Ananya Panday and Alia Bhatt show how the cropped silhouette can be a versatile alternative to full-length trousers for various occasions.

articles.headline: Noel Tata Opposes Public Listing to Preserve Philanthropic Ethos
articles.summary: Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata expressed concern at the HT Leadership Summit that a proposed public listing of Tata Sons by March 2027 could shift focus from philanthropy and long-gestation projects (healthcare, education) to short-term profits. He stated the Trusts will work with regulators to maintain their founding values and current institutional structure, prioritizing national importance over public listing.

articles.headline: Mekedatu Project: Karnataka-Tamil Nadu Water Dispute Intensifies
articles.summary: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar urged the Centre to expedite the Mekedatu reservoir project, stating it's essential for Bengaluru's water and assuring Tamil Nadu its 177 tmc ft Cauvery share. This intensifies political confrontation with TN parties, including Congress and DMK, who vow to block it, exposing national Congress divisions. The CM dismissed opposition as motivated and invited a TN delegation.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi: India's Democracy Destroyed Since 2014 by 'Fascists'
articles.summary: At the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, Rahul Gandhi alleged India's democracy was destroyed in 2014, claiming the BJP weakened institutions and the electoral system with money power and divisive politics. He cited alleged 2024 Lok Sabha poll irregularities, including 140 million voter deletions, and described the fight as against 'fascists,' predicting Modi's defeat. He also apologized for visa denials to delegates.

articles.headline: Manipur Naga Body Issues Ultimatum Over Killings, Demands NIA Probe
articles.summary: The Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL) issued a three-day ultimatum to the Centre and Manipur government, demanding Kuki militants be removed from Naga areas and an NIA probe into the killing of four Nagas in Ukhrul. Blaming authorities for failing to protect civilians, TNL threatens indefinite agitation, while senior Naga leaders call for reconciliation amid the ongoing ethnic crisis.

articles.headline: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Youngest Men's T20 Captain at 15
articles.summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi became the youngest captain in men's T20 history, leading Bihar in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy against Saurashtra at 15 years and 232 days. He surpassed Croatia’s Zach Vukusic's record and earlier became India’s youngest men’s T20 cricketer.

articles.headline: Lakshya Sen Reaches Kumamoto Masters Final
articles.summary: Indian shuttler Lakshya Sen reached the men's singles final at the Kumamoto Masters Japan after a three-game victory (21-12, 15-21, 21-11) over Indonesia's Alwi Farhan. This marks his second consecutive, third overall final this season, boosting his chances for the BWF World Tour Finals and a top-eight ranking. He will face Japan's Koki Watanabe in the summit clash.

articles.headline: India Wins U-19 Asia Cup in Last-Ball Thriller vs Pakistan
articles.summary: India defeated Pakistan by one wicket in a thrilling last-ball finish to win the U-19 Asia Cup in Al Ameerat, Oman, marking their record ninth title. Chasing 338 (or 252), India was struggling before Mohit Ulva's unbeaten 49 off 26 balls, including a final-ball boundary, and Manal Chauhan (47) secured the highest successful chase in Youth ODI history. Pakistan's Usman Khan had scored a century.

articles.headline: David Warner Accuses Cricket Australia of Sandpapergate Cover-up
articles.summary: Former Australian opener David Warner accused Cricket Australia of a "botched," "rushed," and "shoddy" investigation into the 2018 'Sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal, calling it a "cover-up." He alleged CA predetermined blame, ignored key witnesses including major fast bowlers, and sought to blame only three players, preventing him a fair hearing and renewing controversy following Usman Khawaja's comments.

articles.headline: Trump, Putin, Xi to Hold Historic Nuclear Arms Summit
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping are scheduled for an unprecedented trilateral meeting on Nov 19 in Shenzhen (or St. Petersburg) during APEC. Trump will discuss global security, the war in Ukraine, and nuclear arms reduction, aiming to restore prestige and potentially shifting the post-WWII international order.

articles.headline: Akhilesh Yadav: SP to Contest 181 UP Seats, Congress Demands 181
articles.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav announced at the HT Leadership Summit that SP will contest 181 of 403 seats in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. He confirmed the alliance with Congress is intact, though Congress demanded 181 seats. Yadav stressed winning capability over seat count to defeat BJP via a "PDA" coalition of backward classes, Dalits, and minorities.

articles.headline: PM Unveils ₹3,000 Crore Tribal Development Projects on Gaurav Diwas
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay foundation stones for 246 tribal development projects worth ₹3,000 crore on Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas. These initiatives, including 57 Eklavya Model Residential Schools and various infrastructure, health, and multi-purpose centres under the PM-JANMAN scheme, aim to strengthen education, healthcare, and livelihoods for tribal communities across 11 states.

articles.headline: Microsoft Restores Cloud Services After Global Outage
articles.summary: Microsoft fully restored its cloud services, including Teams, 365, Outlook, and Copilot AI, after a major global outage disrupted businesses across the US, Europe, and Asia. The company attributed the widespread failure to a technical fault during a network change and upgrade, ruling out a cyberattack, which highlighted global reliance on centralized digital infrastructure.

articles.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Spy & Affair Allegations
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang abruptly resigned amid reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a senior lawyer in its China operations, linked to an alleged spy scandal. Facing scrutiny from U.S. Congress, calls for his resignation due to professional misconduct and security risks mounted. Huang apologized for the distraction, maintaining company decisions were unaffected, marking a stunning fall for the AI hardware giant's co-founder.

articles.headline: Parliament Security Breach Accused Denied Bail Again Under UAPA
articles.summary: A Delhi court denied bail for the second time to Neelam Azad, Sagar Sharma, and Manoranjan D., accused in the December 2023 Parliament security breach. The judge ruled their acts aimed to spread terror and threaten India's sovereignty, citing prima facie evidence of conspiracy and the statutory bar under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), rendering them unfit for bail.

articles.headline: Bangladesh Completes Legal Steps to Extradite Sheikh Hasina from India
articles.summary: Bangladesh has finalized legal steps to formally request the extradition of former PM Sheikh Hasina from India, where she fled in August 2024. Hasina faces charges including human rights violations and a death sentence by the ICT. While India awaits the next step, considering it a legal matter, Dhaka calls her a "terrorist" and won't issue a passport, raising concerns about potential destabilization and political tensions upon her return.

articles.headline: Deadly Bus Collision in Punjab Kills Five, Injures Fifteen
articles.summary: Five people were killed and 15 injured in Punjab's Tarn Taran district when two pilgrimage buses collided head-on during heavy fog; one driver veered to avoid a motorcycle. PM Modi expressed grief, announcing ex-gratia compensation. The injured were shifted to local hospitals, with critical cases referred to Amritsar.

articles.headline: US Proposes Ukraine Cede Donbas for NATO Membership
articles.summary: US officials have reportedly proposed Ukraine cede the Donbas region to Russia in exchange for immediate NATO membership, aiming for a swift end to the war and long-term security. Kyiv's President Zelensky opposes conceding territory but would consider a national referendum if comprehensive security guarantees and rebuilding funds are offered, facing strong opposition from his leadership.

articles.headline: Voyager 1 Nears 1 Light-Day Milestone from Earth
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft, launched in 1977, is nearing the historic milestone of being one light-day (over 26 billion km) from Earth this Wednesday. Humanity's first object to reach this interstellar distance, its longevity provides unique insights from outside our solar system, continuing to send data deeper into space.

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi Unveils Telangana Gig Worker Welfare Scheme
articles.summary: Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi launched the Telangana Gig Workers’ Social Security and Welfare scheme, promising ₹5 lakh accident and ₹10 lakh health insurance. Funded by a 2% (or 1%) cess on platform deliveries (Uber, Zomato), the initiative also includes Wi-Fi enabled rest zones in Hyderabad and other cities, fulfilling a Congress promise to protect platform-based economy workers.

articles.headline: Pakistan Minister to Visit India for SCO Civilisational Dialogue
articles.summary: Pakistan's federal minister, Musadik Masood Malik, a critic of India's Indus Waters Treaty stance, will visit New Delhi from Nov 20-22 for the inaugural SCO Civilisational Dialogue. This marks the first ministerial visit between the countries since May 2023, signaling a continued effort for dialogue amidst bilateral tensions, despite India having invited a different representative initially.

articles.headline: Supriya Sule: NCP Merger Talks Ended With Ajit Pawar's Death
articles.summary: NCP (Sharad Pawar) MP Supriya Sule declared that merger talks between NCP factions ended with her cousin Ajit Pawar's death in an aircraft accident on January 28. She categorically ruled out joining the NDA, stating no proposal was received, despite rival faction leaders meeting senior BJP figures and Praful Patel meeting her on parliamentary committees, putting a "full stop" to speculation.

articles.headline: Quad Leaders to Hold First Summit Since 2024 in Manila
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi, U.S. President Donald Trump, Japan's PM Sanae Takaichi, and Australia's PM Anthony Albanese will meet on Nov 17 (Tuesday) in Manila for the first Quad summit since 2024, held on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. This historic meeting in a non-member country will address supply chains for critical minerals, commercial shipping lanes, and ship safety.

articles.headline: Karnataka Urges Centre to Protect SC/ST Quota in Ninth Schedule
articles.summary: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar and Deputy CM G. Parameshwara urged the Union government to amend the Constitution, including the Ninth Schedule, to protect the state's enhanced SC/ST reservation law (17% for SCs, 7% for STs, totaling 56%). Citing Tamil Nadu's 69% precedent, they seek to override a High Court ruling that struck down the quota for exceeding the 50% ceiling.

articles.headline: India-Nepal Train to Link Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya
articles.summary: Indian Railways will launch a new 604 km weekly train service connecting Janakpur Dham in Nepal (Sita's birthplace) with Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh (Lord Ram's birthplace). Approved by the railway ministry, this service aims to strengthen cultural, historical, and social bonds, building on cross-border railway discussions, and promote religious tourism.

articles.headline: M. John Harrison Wins Booker Prize, Expresses Despair for Humanity
articles.summary: British author M. John Harrison, 81, won the Booker Prize for his novel "The End of Everything," becoming the oldest winner. Once a champion of resistance, Harrison expressed a lost hope for humanity and deepening pessimism in his latest work, challenging sci-fi norms and focusing on form and voice, despite acknowledging people's ongoing fight for change.

articles.headline: SpaceX Starship Test Flight: Booster Catch Aborted, Spacecraft Healthy
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft launched on a pivotal test flight, deploying all satellites. While the booster catch was aborted, the spacecraft is "healthy" and aims for a novel landing back on Earth. A successful recovery of both the Super Heavy booster and Starship would be a milestone for reusable rocket systems, crucial for future space exploration goals.

articles.headline: Nationwide US Ground Stop: Thousands of Flights Cancelled by Tech Snag
articles.summary: Thousands of flights across the U.S. were cancelled due to a nationwide ground stop, the longest in 25 years. A contractor replacing old copper wire in the air traffic control system overloaded antiquated equipment, causing communication and radar gaps. Over 2,500 flights were affected, with officials warning that the widespread travel disruption could last for days.

articles.headline: Gurnoor Brar Joins India Test Squad, Kuldeep Yadav Released
articles.summary: Pacer Gurnoor Brar was added to India's Test squad for the New Zealand series due to favourable conditions, while left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav was released for domestic game time. Wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant also rejoined the squad after recovering from a back injury, proving his fitness. Gurnoor will miss the final ODI against New Zealand.

articles.headline: Harshal Patel Traded to Gujarat Titans for ₹4 Crore
articles.summary: Two-time IPL Purple Cap winner Harshal Patel is set to join Gujarat Titans from Sunrisers Hyderabad in an all-cash trade for ₹4 crore. The 35-year-old pacer moves ahead of the retention deadline for the 2027 IPL season, following his below-par performance for SRH in IPL 2025.

articles.headline: Elina Svitolina Beats Sabalenka, Reaches WTA Finals Semifinal
articles.summary: Ukrainian Elina Svitolina defeated World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 to reach the WTA Finals semifinals, where she will face Linda Noskova. Mirra Andreeva also advanced, beating Diana Shnaider, showcasing strong performances in the elite season-ending event.

articles.headline: Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy Sees Victories for Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
articles.summary: In the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, Tamil Nadu secured a six-run victory over Railways, with Shahrukh Khan (46 n.o.) and R. Rajkumar (31) leading the charge and Gurjapneet Singh defending 11 runs in the final over. Separately, Karnataka defeated Bengal by 19 runs in their T20 campaign opener, thanks to Karun Nair's 53 and Abhilash Shetty's 4/26.

articles.headline: India Beats Bhutan 2-1, Reaches SAFF Championship Final
articles.summary: India defeated Bhutan 2-1, with goals from P.V. Vishnu and Chinglensana Singh, to reach the SAFF Championship final, where they will face archrivals Pakistan. Bhutan's Kinzang Tashi Tobden scored their goal. VAR made its debut, overturning a penalty decision against India, impacting the match.

articles.headline: Espionage Favoured for Ghulam Ahmed Memorial Trophy at Hyderabad Races
articles.summary: Five-year-old gelding Espionage (Mukesh Kumar up), a recent winner, is favoured to score an encore in the M. Ghulam Ahmed Memorial Trophy, the main event at Sunday's Hyderabad races. The 1200-metre race draws attention from local enthusiasts.

articles.headline: Temba Bavuma Set to Extend South Africa Test Captaincy
articles.summary: Temba Bavuma is expected to extend his Test captaincy for South Africa, aiming to continue his strong record of 13 wins in his first 15 Tests. His impressive leadership, including recent victories against Bangladesh, positions him for continued leadership of the national cricket team.

articles.headline: India Dominates Guam 12-0, Qualifies for U-17 Asian Cup Final Stage
articles.summary: India qualified for the U-17 Asian Cup final stage, defeating Guam 12-0 in the AFC U-17 Asian Cup Qualifiers. Raj Singh Wahengbam and Dallalmuon Gangte each scored hat-tricks, along with braces from Boby Singh and Rishikesh, as six different players contributed to the dominant victory, leading their group on goal difference.
